title: finding(types): the `SchemaRegistry` value-vs-renderer sweep (objectui#7665's option A) has no card, while two comments in `registry.ts` name objectui#7665 as holding it — a card that excludes it by name and is about to close
body:
Filed from the in-seat review of PR objectui#9677 (card objectui#7665). The lane reported the symptom; the measurement and the third reading below are the reviewing seat's.

## The work that has no card

objectui#7665's dev seat framed the repair of `SchemaRegistry`'s docblock as **option C** — cheap, prose-only, removing the false expectation. It named **option A** as the only route that closes the class:

> sweep all 60+ keys against their registered renderers and extend the family rule

and its triage instruction is explicit that A is not C's to do:

> ⚠️ Do **not** fold in a sweep of the other keys. That is option A and belongs on its own card with its own measurement.

**Option A has never been filed.** This card is it, so the work has an owner and an address.

## And two comments already point at the wrong one

Measured on `main` at `72f55c9ec`, `packages/types/src/registry.ts` carries two comments that name objectui#7665 as the card that HOLDS the sweep:

| line | text |
|---|---|
| `:233` | *"That is the objectui#7665 **sweep's territory** (this map's coverage), not this retirement's"* |
| `:272` | *"it is NOT a sweep of the map's other entries, **which objectui#7665 holds**"* |

objectui#7665 does not hold it — its own body and its triage comment both exclude it by name. ⇒ Those two comments route a reader to a card for work that card refuses, and once objectui#7665 closes (PR objectui#9677 does that) they route to a **closed** card. The reader's next move after following either one is to conclude the sweep was done.

⭐ Worth stating plainly because it is the reason this card exists rather than a tidy-up: **those two comments are currently the only thing in the tree that remembers this work exists.** Retarget them at this card as part of doing it.

## What the sweep is

For each key in `SchemaRegistry` (measured: **70** members on `72f55c9ec`), compare the declared value type against the type the registered renderer actually honours, and record the divergences. The family rule the card refers to is the discriminator that explains why a divergence is or is not a defect:

- an entry whose renderer lives in THIS package can and must name the honoured type;
- an entry whose renderer lives in a plugin package **cannot** — `pnpm check:phantom-deps` judges `import type` exactly as a value import (`scripts/check-phantom-dependencies.mjs:127`, *"Type-only imports are STRICT"*) and declaring the dependency closes a cycle. For those, the limit is this layer's reach and the remedy is a move in the plugin, not a wider claim here (objectui#7664 did exactly that for kanban).

PR objectui#9677 writes that discriminator into the docblock. This card applies it key by key.

## Known member of the population, already measured

`:233` records one: this map has **never** carried an `'object-kanban'` entry, and since the bare `'kanban'` key was retired (objectui#8802, maintainer ruling 2026-09-09) the kanban family has **no entry at all**. ⚠️ That one is a KEY-SET question, not a value divergence, and adding an entry widens `ComponentType` — which the file itself calls a ruling. ⛔ It is not this card's to decide unilaterally; it is this card's to surface.

## Cost, stated because it is why option C went first

The dev seat's framing: option A's cost *"is unbounded until someone measures how many diverge"*. ⇒ A grader may want this split in two — a measuring pass that produces the divergence count, and a fixing pass priced against it. ⛔ This card asserts no count; nobody has taken one.

## Not measured here

⛔ How many of the 70 entries diverge. ⛔ Whether any divergence outside the kanban one is reachable by an author. ⛔ Whether the same two-comment staleness exists in sibling maps — only `registry.ts` was read.

Refs: objectui#7665 (option C, the docblock split) - PR objectui#9677 - objectui#7645 (the worked example) - objectui#7664 (the plugin-side resolution) - objectui#8802 (the `kanban` retirement) - objectui#7704 (the two chatbot keys, explicitly not a sweep).
